title: Kenyan Grilled Vegetable Platter
community: Urban Kenya — the restaurant vegetarian showcase
author: Chef Amina Hassan
desc: Kenyan Grilled Vegetable Platter — colourful seasonal vegetables charred over high heat until smoky and tender, drizzled with herb oil, lemon, and pili pili. A vegetarian showpiece that celebrates Kenya's diverse and high-quality vegetable production.
longDesc: Kenya's vegetable production is exceptional — the fertile highlands produce capsicums, courgettes, aubergines, mushrooms, and asparagus of extraordinary quality. Grilled over high heat with herb oil, they become smoky, tender, and deeply satisfying.
steps: Make herb oil: combine olive oil, garlic, herbs, lemon, and salt.
Brush all vegetables with herb oil.
Heat grill pan or charcoal grill to high heat.
Grill each vegetable until char marks form and they are tender — capsicums 4—5 min per side; courgette and aubergine 3—4 min; asparagus 2—3 min; mushrooms 4—5 min.
Drizzle with remaining herb oil and pili pili sauce.
chefTips: High heat is the key — low heat produces steamed, not grilled, vegetables.
Do not move vegetables immediately after placing — let them develop char marks.
Arrange by colour for restaurant-level visual impact.
commonMistakes: Low heat — no char, no smoke, no flavour.
Moving too early — prevents char mark development.
cookingScience: The characteristic smoky flavour of grilled vegetables comes from partial combustion of surface sugars and the deposition of volatile compounds from the grill smoke. Aubergine contains air pockets in its flesh that collapse during grilling — this is why properly grilled aubergine becomes dramatically tender.
sustainabilityTips: Kenya's highlands produce an extraordinary range of vegetables year-round with minimal inputs.
servedWith: As a side to Mixed Grill (KEN251)
reheating: Warm briefly in a hot pan.
healthBenefits: Multiple vegetables provide diverse vitamins and phytochemicals.
culturalNote: The grilled vegetable platter demonstrates the breadth of Kenya's agricultural production — a showcase of the country's vegetable-growing excellence that stands proud alongside the meat dishes.
